title: Policy namespace and admin guardrails for multi-tenant resource plane
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a Policy Namespace and Admin Guardrails layer for RBAC v2. This ticket covers: a namespaced policy surface for multi-tenant resources (policy namespaces per-tenant and per-environment), a minimal Principal surface for SSO/SAML group -> role mapping, an immutable audit event schema for permission grants and admin actions, and runtime guardrails (break-glass, time-limited elevation, approval workflows) to reduce blast radius for admin operations. The goal is to enable predictable least-privilege assignments across hosted/dedicated/private deployments and provide a migration path from existing RBAC v1 role blobs.
background: Current RBAC implementation is a flat role-assignment model with tenant-scoped roles encoded as free-form blobs. This causes: fragile permission combinatorics across resources, unclear audit trails for elevation events, and brittle SSO mappings. Customers with Dedicated/Private deployments have asked for clearer separation of admin planes, predictable inheritance across resource hierarchies, and auditable temporary elevations. Security and compliance require a stable audit event schema and tamper-resistant record retention. RBAC v2 will introduce a namespaced policy model, explicit scope anchors, and admin guardrails to satisfy these requirements.
proposal: 1) Introduce Policy Namespace as the top-level container: formats 'tenant:<tenant_id>' and optional 'env:<tenant_id>:<env>' for isolated staging/prod policies. 2) Principal surface: canonicalize identities into 'user:<id>', 'service:<id>', 'group:<id>' produced by SSO mapping. 3) Permission tuples use 'resource_type:resource_id:scope' with explicit inheritance rules. 4) Admin guardrails: pre-defined immutable admin roles (e.g., org-admin, infra-admin) with safe defaults, mandatory MFA for admin grants, time-limited elevation tokens (TTL-based), and a break-glass flow requiring approval and emits high-fidelity audit events. 5) Audit: standardize event schema (versioned v1) and route to kafka topic 'audit.events.rbac.v1' and long-term storage with append-only retention for Private deployments. 6) Migration: compatibility layer that maps existing role blobs to policy namespace and emits a dry-run log to validate mappings before cutover.
design_decisions:
- Namespacing prevents cross-tenant role collisions and simplifies policy lookup.
- We prefer explicit scope anchors over wildcard inheritance except for legacy compatibility.
- Time-limited elevation will be implemented as signed JWT tokens with stapled audit reference IDs.
- SSO mapping: allow both 'group-to-role' and 'attribute-to-role' transforms; prefer signed assertions from IdPs for critical admin mappings.
- Audit schema includes actor, principal_type, action, resource_tuple, policy_version, decision, request_id, and tamper-proof hash.
- Rollout strategy: feature-flagged per-tenant with a canary cohort (10 internal teams) then customers opt-in for migration.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Strict namespaces add operational overhead for small tenants; mitigated via tooling that auto-generates default namespaces.
- Immutable admin roles reduce flexibility for edge-cases; we provide 'delegated-admin' templates for controlled delegation.
- Time-limited elevation requires clock sync and token revocation hooks; we will add revocation via a short-lived cache + audit index.
- Migration carries risk of permission regression; plan includes dry-run mapping, automated policy diff reports, and a reversible compatibility layer for 30 days.
migration_plan: 1) Build mapping tool that reads RBAC v1 blobs and emits candidate policy namespace mappings and a human-readable diff. 2) Run dry-run on internal accounts and 3 early access customers. 3) Add a compatibility read-layer that answers legacy queries by translating to RBAC v2 policy checks for 30 days post-cutover. 4) Provide CLI/Console inspector to show mapped policies and allow one-click manual adjustments. 5) After validation window, flip default evaluation order to RBAC v2 and deprecate compatibility layer with a 90-day notice.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy Namespace implemented and queryable via API; documentation published.
- Principal canonicalization implemented for SSO flows; mappings testable in staging.
- Admin guardrail flows: MFA-enforced grant, time-limited elevation tokens, and break-glass approval flow function end-to-end in canary tenants.
- Audit event schema v1 implemented, events emitted to kafka topic and visible in Console logs with request_id correlation.
- Migration tool produces mapping diffs for 3 internal tenants and 2 EA customers with zero high-severity regressions.
- Load tests: policy evaluation latency at p95 remains under 8ms for cached checks and under 25ms for cold evaluations.
- Security review completed with sign-off and threat model updated.

Canonicalize principal surface and SAML group/attribute mappers
Implement token-based time-limited elevation service and revocation index
Wire audit producer to kafka and long-term storage with append-only mode
Build migration mapper and console inspector UI
Create canary rollout plan and automated policy diff reports
Run perf and load tests and document latency targets
notes:
- Prototype for time-limited elevation exists in PR #1293 (github).
- Security has requested an additional attestation field in audit schema (see links).
- We will reuse existing KV cache key patterns for policy evaluation cache but namespace the keys to support tenant isolation.
- Consider future work: policy templating, quota-scoped permissions, and external policy-as-code integrations.
